title: Oxford 5000 (CEFR B2-C1)
subtitle: Advanced Communicative Fluency & Nuance
citation: Oxford University Press (2019). The Oxford 5000: An expanded core vocabulary for advanced learners of English aligned with CEFR.
description: Selected from Oxford University Press's 2.5-billion-word English Corpus. These B2-C1 headwords bridge the gap between basic communicative adequacy and articulate, nuanced expression.

words.definition: To publicly recommend or support a particular cause, policy, or action.
words.example: Public health experts advocate for stricter limits on industrial carbon emissions.

words.definition: Including or dealing with all or nearly all elements or aspects of something.
words.example: The committee published a comprehensive survey analyzing graduate employment trends.

words.definition: To recognize or ascertain what makes someone or something distinct.
words.example: Startups must differentiate their offerings in an increasingly saturated software market.

words.definition: To make an action or process easy, smoother, or more efficient.
words.example: Modern digital platforms facilitate cross-functional collaboration across disparate time zones.

words.definition: A system in which members of an organization or society are ranked according to relative status.
words.example: The executive team flattened the corporate hierarchy to accelerate operational decision-making.

words.definition: To put a decision, plan, or agreement into practical effect.
words.example: The municipal council voted to implement new municipal water conservation guidelines.

words.definition: A thing that motivates, stimulates, or encourages someone to take action.
words.example: Targeted tax incentives encourage commercial enterprises to adopt renewable energy.

words.definition: To combine one thing with another so that they become a functional whole.
words.example: The engineering curriculum integrates computational simulations with empirical lab experiments.

words.definition: To demonstrate or display a quality, feeling, or condition clearly by actions or symptoms.
words.example: Chronic occupational stress can manifest through physical fatigue and reduced concentration.

words.definition: A remarkable fact or situation that is observed to exist, especially one whose cause is investigated.
words.example: Bioluminescence in deep-sea organisms remains an extraordinary biological phenomenon.

words.definition: To strengthen or support an object, concept, or argument with additional evidence.
words.example: Subsequent peer-reviewed studies reinforce the original conclusions of the climate model.

words.definition: Able to be maintained at a steady rate or level without depleting natural resources.
words.example: City planners released an ambitious framework for sustainable public transit expansion.
